page: Vultr vhp-2c-4gb-amd is a shared-core virtual private server belonging to the High Performance family. It features 2 vCPUs mapped to 1 physical AMD EPYC core with 2 threads per core, running at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz. The system is equipped with 4.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB of RAM per core. For local storage, it includes a bundled 100 GB NVMe SSD. The CPU architecture is x86_64 and supports instruction sets such as AVX, AES, SHA_NI, and FMA, though it lacks AVX-512 capabilities.

Benchmark results indicate entry-level performance characteristics. The single-core stress-ng CPU performance is rated as average with a score of 2318.46, but multi-core performance drops to the weak category at 4565.57. Memory bandwidth tests show weak throughput, with read-only large block speeds at 25.27 GB/sec and write speeds at 21.3 GB/sec. Real-world application benchmarks demonstrate poor to weak performance, including a Geekbench single-core score of 1021.0, a multi-core score of 1821.0, and static web serving throughput of 2.03 GB/sec. Redis SET operations reach 2.1 million operations per second, which falls into the lower performance tier.

Given its shared CPU allocation and modest memory capacity, this server type offers a cost-effective entry point for workloads with low resource density. The bundled 100 GB NVMe SSD provides fast local storage relative to the compute tier, but the shared CPU model presents a tradeoff in sustained multi-threaded performance. This configuration is best suited for lightweight workloads such as basic web serving, development environments, low-traffic database operations, or simple background utility tasks.
